description: VA-1/W5 IQ consistency subset: served IQ runs (external controller process in barrier mode, external RX app, 10 ms windows) vs the batch evaluators over 1000 s
assumptions: acceptance (noise off): |IQ - vectorized midpoint evaluator| <= 0.02 dB
acceptance (noise on): vectorized value inside the IQ 95 % batch-means interval (20 batches)
run_batch (left-point rule, 5 ms grid) reported for comparison
VA-1 verdict only over the complete design: every (controller, tau_SUI, noise) row, 1000 s each
rows may come from several hosts ('hosts'; cpu_model and platform per row): wall time and RTF are host-specific, powers are not

files.va1.csv: one row per (controller, tau_SUI, noise), with host and code provenance

exact_tau0.1_noiseoff.origin: lead AWS job (research/aws/runner.py): bundle of the sremu repo, outputs under $SREMU_JOB_OUT, returned as results.tgz
exact_tau0.1_noiseoff.note: Imported by the WP11 finalize track on 2026-10-11. The laptop runs of these four points (AMD Ryzen 9 8945H, Windows 11) did not finish: the driver's 600 s server wait timed out (runs/wp11/ea_iq_exact_0.1.log, ea_iq_urap_0.1.log), so the rows were measured on AWS. Bundle = git archive of HEAD at launch plus extra working-tree paths, without .git, so the manifests record git_commit null. HEAD at launch (23:28:22Z) was b4247316 (committed 23:26:44Z); src/ is identical in b4247316 and f518ed1 (git diff). The 12 driver and scenario files whose SHA-256 the job recorded (experiments/*.py, scenarios/studies/ea_corridor.yaml, scenarios/lab_like_A.yaml) equal their versions committed in f518ed1. The job's src_sremu_tree_sha256 (d61b9664...) differs from f518ed1's (8335241f...), so the bundle carried at least one extra untracked src file that the returned results do not identify.
exact_tau0.1_noiseoff.job_cmd: python -m experiments.ea_iq run --out $SREMU_JOB_OUT/ea_iq --cache /opt/job/cache --only exact:0.1; python -m experiments.ea_iq run --out $SREMU_JOB_OUT/ea_iq --cache /opt/job/cache --only urap:0.1; python -c "from experiments.ef import run_latency; import json; print(json.dumps(run_latency('$SREMU_JOB_OUT/ef_latency'), default=str)[:4000])"
